text: The pitching the first wicket is to be determined by the cast of a piece of money.
text_norm: the pitching the first wicket is to be determined by the cast of a piece of money.

text: When the first wicket is pitch’d, and the popping-crease cut, which must be exactly three feet ten inches from the wicket, the other wicket is to be pitch’d directly opposite at twenty-two yards distance, and the either popping-crease cut three feet ten inches before it.
text_norm: when the first wicket is pitch'd, and the popping-crease cut, which must be exactly three feet ten inches from the wicket, the other wicket is to be pitch'd directly opposite at twenty-two yards distance, and the either popping-crease cut three feet ten inches before it.

text: The bowling-creases must be cut in a direct line from each stump.
text_norm: the bowling-creases must be cut in a direct line from each stump.

text: The stumps must be twenty-two inches long, and the bail six inches.
text_norm: the stumps must be twenty-two inches long, and the bail six inches.

text: The ball must weigh between five and six ounces.
text_norm: the ball must weigh between five and six ounces.

text: When the wickets are both pitch’d, and all the creases cut, the party that wins the toss-up may order which side shall go in first, at his option.
text_norm: when the wickets are both pitch'd, and all the creases cut, the party that wins the toss-up may order which side shall go in first, at his option.

text: The LAWS for the BOWLERS Four balls and over The bowler must deliver the ball, with one foot behind the crease, even with the wicket: and when he has bowled one ball or more, shall bowl to the number four before he changes wickets, and he shall change but once in the same innings.
text_norm: the laws for the bowlers four balls and over the bowler must deliver the ball, with one foot behind the crease, even with the wicket: and when he has bowled one ball or more, shall bowl to the number four before he changes wickets, and he shall change but once in the same innings.

text: He may order the player that is in at his wicket to stand on which side of it he pleases at a reasonable distance.
text_norm: he may order the player that is in at his wicket to stand on which side of it he pleases at a reasonable distance.

text: If he delivers the ball with his hinder foot over the bowling-crease, the umpire shall call no ball, though she be struck, or the player is bowled out; which he shall do without being ask’d, and no person shall have the right to ask him.
text_norm: if he delivers the ball with his hinder foot over the bowling-crease, the umpire shall call no ball, though she be struck, or the player is bowled out; which he shall do without being ask'd, and no person shall have the right to ask him.

text: LAWS for the STRIKERS, or those that are in If the wicket is bowl’d down, it’s out.
text_norm: laws for the strikers, or those that are in if the wicket is bowl'd down, it's out.

text: If he strikes or treads down, or he falls himself upon the wicket in striking (but not in over-running) it’s out.
text_norm: if he strikes or treads down, or he falls himself upon the wicket in striking (but not in over-running) it's out.

text: A stroke or nip over or under his bat, or upon his hands (but not arms) if the ball be held before she touches ground, though she be hugg’d to the body, it’s out.
text_norm: a stroke or nip over or under his bat, or upon his hands (but not arms) if the ball be held before she touches ground, though she be hugg'd to the body, it's out.

text: If in striking both his feet are over the popping-crease, and his wicket put down, except his bat is down within, it’s out.
text_norm: if in striking both his feet are over the popping-crease, and his wicket put down, except his bat is down within, it's out.

text: If he runs out of his ground to hinder a catch, it’s out.
text_norm: if he runs out of his ground to hinder a catch, it's out.

text: If a ball is nipp’d up, and he strikes her again wilfully before she come to the wicket, it’s out.
text_norm: if a ball is nipp'd up, and he strikes her again wilfully before she come to the wicket, it's out.

text: If the players have cross’d each other, he that runs for the wicket that is put down, is out; if they are not cross’d, he that returns is out.
text_norm: if the players have cross'd each other, he that runs for the wicket that is put down, is out; if they are not cross'd, he that returns is out.

text: If in running a notch, the wicket is struck down by a throw, before his foot, hand, or bat is over the popping-crease, or a stump is hit by the ball, though the bail was down, it’s out.
text_norm: if in running a notch, the wicket is struck down by a throw, before his foot, hand, or bat is over the popping-crease, or a stump is hit by the ball, though the bail was down, it's out.

text: But if the bail is down before, he that catches the ball must strike a stump out of the ground ball in hand, then it’s out.
text_norm: but if the bail is down before, he that catches the ball must strike a stump out of the ground ball in hand, then it's out.

text: If the striker touches, or takes up the ball before she is lain quite still, unless ask’d by the bowler or wicket-keeper, it’s out.
text_norm: if the striker touches, or takes up the ball before she is lain quite still, unless ask'd by the bowler or wicket-keeper, it's out.

text: BAT, FOOT, or HAND over the CREASE When the ball has been in hand by one of the keepers or stoppers, and the player has been at home, he may go where he pleases till the next ball is bowled.
text_norm: bat, foot, or hand over the crease when the ball has been in hand by one of the keepers or stoppers, and the player has been at home, he may go where he pleases till the next ball is bowled.

text: If either of the strikers is cross’d in his running ground designedly, which design must be determined by the umpires.
text_norm: if either of the strikers is cross'd in his running ground designedly, which design must be determined by the umpires.

text: N.B.
text_norm: n.b.

text: The umpires may order that notch to be scored.
text_norm: the umpires may order that notch to be scored.

text: When the ball is hit up, either of the strikers may hinder the catch in his running ground; or if she is hit directly across the wickets, the other player may place his body anywhere within the swing of the bat, so as to hinder the bowler from catching her; but he must neither strike at her, nor touch her with his hands.
text_norm: when the ball is hit up, either of the strikers may hinder the catch in his running ground; or if she is hit directly across the wickets, the other player may place his body anywhere within the swing of the bat, so as to hinder the bowler from catching her; but he must neither strike at her, nor touch her with his hands.

text: If a striker nips a ball up just before him, he may fall before his wicket, or pop down his bat, before she come to it, to save it.
text_norm: if a striker nips a ball up just before him, he may fall before his wicket, or pop down his bat, before she come to it, to save it.

text: The bail hanging on one stump, though the ball hit the wicket, it’s not out. - 5 - LAWS for the WICKET-KEEPERS The wicket-keepers shall stand at a reasonable distance behind the wicket, and shall not move till the ball is out of the bowler’s hand, and shall not by any noise incommode the striker; and if his hands, knees, foot or head, be over or before the wicket, though the ball hit it, it shall not be out.
text_norm: the bail hanging on one stump, though the ball hit the wicket, it's not out. - 5 - laws for the wicket-keepers the wicket-keepers shall stand at a reasonable distance behind the wicket, and shall not move till the ball is out of the bowler's hand, and shall not by any noise incommode the striker; and if his hands, knees, foot or head, be over or before the wicket, though the ball hit it, it shall not be out.

text: LaWS for the UMPIRES To allow two minutes for each man to come in when one is out, and ten minutes between each hand.
text_norm: laws for the umpires to allow two minutes for each man to come in when one is out, and ten minutes between each hand.

text: To mark the ball that it may not be changed.
text_norm: to mark the ball that it may not be changed.

text: They are sole judges of all outs and ins, of all fair or unfair play, of all frivolous delays, of all hurts, whether real or pretended, and are discretionally to allow what time they think proper before the game goes on again.
text_norm: they are sole judges of all outs and ins, of all fair or unfair play, of all frivolous delays, of all hurts, whether real or pretended, and are discretionally to allow what time they think proper before the game goes on again.

text: In case of a real hurt to a striker, they are to allow another to come in, and the person hurt to come in again: but are not to allow a fresh man to play, on either side, on any account.
text_norm: in case of a real hurt to a striker, they are to allow another to come in, and the person hurt to come in again: but are not to allow a fresh man to play, on either side, on any account.

text: They are sole judges of all hindrances, crossing the players in running, and standing unfair to strike, and in cases of hindrance may order a notch to be scored.
text_norm: they are sole judges of all hindrances, crossing the players in running, and standing unfair to strike, and in cases of hindrance may order a notch to be scored.

text: They are not to order any man out, unless appealed to by one of the players.
text_norm: they are not to order any man out, unless appealed to by one of the players.

text: These laws are to the umpires jointly.
text_norm: these laws are to the umpires jointly.

text: Each umpire is the sole judge of all nips and catches, ins and outs, good or bad runs, at his own wicket, and his determination shall be absolute; and he shall not be changed for another umpire, without the consent of both sides.
text_norm: each umpire is the sole judge of all nips and catches, ins and outs, good or bad runs, at his own wicket, and his determination shall be absolute; and he shall not be changed for another umpire, without the consent of both sides.

text: When the four balls are bowl’d, he is to call over.
text_norm: when the four balls are bowl'd, he is to call over.

text: These laws are separately.
text_norm: these laws are separately.

text: When both umpires call play three times, ’tis at the peril of awing the game from them that refuses to play.
text_norm: when both umpires call play three times, 'tis at the peril of awing the game from them that refuses to play.
